symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of independently sampled observational units.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: The fixed dimension of the covariate vector.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: The treatment level indexing potential outcomes and regressions.

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: A generic H\"older smoothness order.

symbols.name: m_u
symbols.type: strict integer part of the smoothness order
symbols.def: \(m_u=\lceil u\rceil-1\), the largest nonnegative integer strictly smaller than \(u\).

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: The H\"older order of the propensity score.

symbols.name: \beta
symbols.def: The H\"older order of the treatment-specific outcome regressions.

symbols.name: \gamma
symbols.def: The H\"older order of the CATE.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: \(s=(\alpha+\beta)/2\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: A fixed envelope for H\"older norms and bounded outcomes.

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: The fixed lower bound on both treatment probabilities.

symbols.name: f_{-}
symbols.def: The fixed positive lower envelope for the covariate density.

symbols.name: f_{+}
symbols.def: The fixed upper envelope for the covariate density.

symbols.name: x_0
symbols.def: A fixed interior covariate value at which the CATE is evaluated.

symbols.name: Y(0)
symbols.def: The potential outcome under control.

symbols.name: Y(1)
symbols.def: The potential outcome under treatment.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: The observed binary treatment.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The observed pre-treatment covariate vector.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The realized outcome.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: A law for the potential outcomes and the observed data.

symbols.name: f_P
symbols.def: The Lebesgue density of \(X\) under \(P\).

symbols.name: \pi_P
symbols.def: \(\pi_P(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x)\).

symbols.name: \mu_{a,P}
symbols.def: \(\mu_{a,P}(x)=\mathbb{E}_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\).

symbols.name: \mathcal{H}^{u}_d(L)
symbols.def: The radius-\(L\) isotropic H\"older ball of order \(u\), constructed in \(\mathrm{def:holder-ball}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{low}}
symbols.def: The strict smoothness region constructed in \(\mathrm{def:low-smoothness-region}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band},n}
symbols.space: sets of full-data laws indexed by \(n\)
symbols.def: The primitive causal law class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:band-class}\).

symbols.name: R_n^{\mathrm{band}}
symbols.def: The pointwise CATE minimax risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:band-risk}\).

symbols.name: r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}
symbols.def: The published density-qualified pointwise CATE benchmark constructed in \(\mathrm{def:kbrw-rate}\).

symbols.name: r_n^{\mathrm{band}}
symbols.def: The candidate polynomial minimax rate constructed in \(\mathrm{def:band-rate}\).

symbols.name: \overline r_n^{\mathrm{band}}
symbols.def: The logarithmically inflated upper rate constructed in \(\mathrm{def:band-upper-rate}\).

symbols.name: k_n
symbols.def: \(k_n=\lfloor n/(\log n)^2\rfloor\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{cap}}_n(x_0)
symbols.space: measurable functions of \(O_{1:n}\) with values in \(\mathbb{R}\)
symbols.def: The cross-fitted estimator constructed in \(\mathrm{def:rank-capped-estimator}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak{H}^{\mathrm{dens}}_n
symbols.space: unproved density, propensity, and regression perturbation-and-mixture programs over laws in \(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band},n}\)
symbols.def: The candidate positive-band testing program named in \(\mathrm{def:density\mbox{-}coupled\mbox{-}handle}\); it is not a delivered lower-bound construction.

symbols.name: \mathfrak{H}^{\mathrm{asym}}
symbols.space: estimator and testing programs over band-only CATE experiments
symbols.def: The route for the unresolved exact frontier constructed in \(\mathrm{def:asymmetric-frontier-handle}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{pair}}
symbols.def: The band-only close-pair region constructed by the close-pair-region definition.

symbols.name: \widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{pair}}_n(x_0)
symbols.space: measurable functions of \(O_{1:n}\) with values in \(\mathbb R\)
symbols.def: The total pair-difference estimator constructed by the close-pair estimator definition.

definitions.name: \mathcal{H}^{u}_d(L)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{H}^{u}_d(L)=\left\{g:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb{R}:\max_{|v|\le m_u}\lVert D^v g\rVert_\infty\le L,\ \max_{|v|=m_u}\sup_{x\ne x'}\frac{|D^v g(x)-D^v g(x')|}{\lVert x-x'\rVert_2^{u-m_u}}\le L\right\},\qquad m_u=\lceil u\rceil-1.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band},n}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band},n}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L,\varepsilon,f_{-},f_{+},x_0)=\left\{P:\text{for this }n\in\mathbb{N},\text{ every member property enumerated below holds}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: R_n^{\mathrm{band}}
definitions.construction: \[R_n^{\mathrm{band}}=\inf_{T_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band},n}}\mathbb{E}_P\left|T_n(O_{1:n})-\tau_P(x_0)\right|,\] where the infimum is over all measurable estimators \(T_n\).

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{cap}}_n(x_0)
definitions.construction:
For every \(v\in\{\alpha,\beta\}\), put
\[
q_v=\binom{d+\lceil v\rceil-1}{d}.
\]
For \(n<3\), define \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cap}}(x_0)=0\).  For
\(n\geq3\), if \(q_\alpha>k_n\), if \(q_\beta>k_n\), or if for either
\(v\in\{\alpha,\beta\}\) there is no positive integer \(m\) satisfying
\(q_vm^d\leq k_n\), again define the whole estimator to be zero.  Otherwise,
let
\[
m_v=\max\{m\in\mathbb N:q_vm^d\leq k_n\}.
\]
Partition \([0,1]^d\) into the regular \(m_v^d\) tensor cells, using
half-open cells except at the upper boundary.  On each cell, orthonormalize
the monomials of total degree at most \(\lceil v\rceil-1\) in graded
lexicographic order with positive leading coefficient, and order the cells
lexicographically.  Extending every cell polynomial by zero off its cell
gives a deterministic Lebesgue-orthonormal vector \(B_{v,n}\) of dimension
\(q_vm_v^d\leq k_n\).

Write \(n=3b+r\), where \(b=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\) and
\(r\in\{0,1,2\}\), and set
\[
N_j=b+\mathbf 1\{j\leq r\},\qquad
I_1=\{1,\ldots,N_1\},\quad
I_2=\{N_1+1,\ldots,N_1+N_2\},\quad
I_3=\{N_1+N_2+1,\ldots,n\}.
\]
Subscripts on these folds are read modulo three in \(\{1,2,3\}\).  For a
fold \(J\), define
\[
G_{v,J}=\frac1{|J|}\sum_{i\in J}B_{v,n}(X_i)B_{v,n}(X_i)^\top,
\qquad
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{nuis}}(G)
=U\operatorname{diag}\!\left(
\min\{2f_+,\max\{f_-/2,\lambda_j\}\}
\right)U^\top
\]
when \(G=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_j)U^\top\).  In cyclic fit
\(r\in\{1,2,3\}\), use \(I_r\) to form
\[
\widetilde\pi_{r,a}(x)=B_{\alpha,n}(x)^\top
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{nuis}}(G_{\alpha,I_r})^{-1}
\frac1{|I_r|}\sum_{i\in I_r}B_{\alpha,n}(X_i)A_i,
\]
and use the independent fold \(I_{r+1}\) to form the analogous
\(\widetilde\pi_{r,b}\) and
\[
\widetilde\eta_r(x)=B_{\beta,n}(x)^\top
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{nuis}}(G_{\beta,I_{r+1}})^{-1}
\frac1{|I_{r+1}|}\sum_{i\in I_{r+1}}B_{\beta,n}(X_i)Y_i.
\]
Put
\[
\widehat\pi_{r,a}=\operatorname{clip}_{[\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]}
(\widetilde\pi_{r,a}),\qquad
\widehat\pi_{r,b}=\operatorname{clip}_{[\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]}
(\widetilde\pi_{r,b}),\qquad
\widehat\eta_r=\operatorname{clip}_{[-2,2]}(\widetilde\eta_r).
\]
The enlarged clipping intervals leave a fixed buffer around the true ranges
\([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) and \([-1,1]\).

Let \(\mathcal C=[-1/2,1/2]^d\), let \(b_\gamma\) be the vector obtained by
orthonormalizing, in graded lexicographic order with positive leading
coefficient, the polynomials on \(\mathcal C\) of total degree at most
\(\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\), and set
\[
b_{i,h}=b_\gamma((X_i-x_0)/h_n),\qquad
K_{i,h}=h_n^{-d}\mathbf1\{(X_i-x_0)/h_n\in\mathcal C\}.
\]
On the evaluation fold \(I_{r+2}\), form
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat Q_r&=\frac1{|I_{r+2}|}\sum_{i\in I_{r+2}}
K_{i,h}b_{i,h}b_{i,h}^\top
\{A_i-\widehat\pi_{r,a}(X_i)\}
\{A_i-\widehat\pi_{r,b}(X_i)\},\\
\widehat S_r&=\frac1{|I_{r+2}|}\sum_{i\in I_{r+2}}
K_{i,h}b_{i,h}
\{A_i-\widehat\pi_{r,a}(X_i)\}
\{Y_i-\widehat\eta_r(X_i)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For a symmetric matrix \(Q=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_j)U^\top\), define
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{loc}}(Q)=U\operatorname{diag}\!\left(
\min\{2f_+,\max\{\varepsilon^2f_-/2,\lambda_j\}\}
\right)U^\top.
\]
Let
\[
\widehat\theta_r=\mathsf C_{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat Q_r)^{-1}
\widehat S_r,
\qquad
\widehat t_r=b_\gamma(0)^\top\widehat\theta_r,
\]
and define \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cap}}(x_0)\) as the truncation to
\([-2,2]\) of \(3^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^3\widehat t_r\).  The two spectral maps
are independent of the choice of eigenvectors on repeated eigenspaces.
Together with the fixed ordering, boundary convention, explicit fallbacks,
and consecutive folds above, this is a total measurable function of
\(O_{1:n}\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak{H}^{\mathrm{dens}}_n
definitions.construction:
The symbol \(\mathfrak H_n^{\mathrm{dens}}\) names the following candidate
positive-band testing program.  Start from the uniform density, which lies
strictly inside \([f_{-},f_{+}]\), partition a shrinking cube around \(x_0\)
into paired cells, place normalized mean-zero signed wavelet perturbations in
\(f_P\), couple their signs with flat-top perturbations of \(\pi_P\) and
\(\mu_{a,P}\), and mix over the paired signs.  The cell widths and amplitudes
are to be chosen subject to H\"older membership, density normalization, the
fixed two-sided density band, target separation, and an \(n\)-sample testing-distance
bound.  This notation specifies only the candidate perturbation-and-mixture
program; model membership, separation, and indistinguishability are analytical
properties that require separate theorem proofs.

definitions.name: \mathfrak{H}^{\mathrm{asym}}
definitions.construction: The symbol \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{asym}}\) names the following open-problem program: combine same-sample M\"obius-stabilized Gram corrections at distinct propensity and outcome-regression resolutions with unequal-resolution, mean-zero density perturbations that remain normalized inside \([f_{-},f_{+}]\).  A successful resolution would have to verify the estimator risk and, separately, full model membership, target separation, and an \(n\)-sample testing-distance bound.  This definition asserts none of those conclusions.

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{pair}}_n(x_0)
definitions.construction:
Put \(\mathcal C=[-1/2,1/2]^d\), and let
\(\kappa(z)=\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal C\}=\prod_{r=1}^d
\mathbf 1\{|z_r|\leq1/2\}\).  If
\((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\notin\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\), define
\(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{pair}}(x_0)=0\).  Otherwise set
\[
s=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2},\qquad
t=\left(1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{4s}\right)^{-1},
\qquad h=n^{-t/\gamma},\qquad \ell=n^{-t/(2s)}.
\]
Let
\[
\delta_0=\min_{1\leq r\leq d}\{x_{0,r},1-x_{0,r}\},
\qquad
K_h(z)=h^{-d}\kappa(z/h),
\qquad K_\ell(z)=\ell^{-d}\kappa(z/\ell).
\]
Orthonormalize, for Lebesgue measure on \(\mathcal C\), the monomials of
total degree at most \(\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\), in graded lexicographic order
and with positive leading coefficient; denote the resulting deterministic
column vector by \(b_\gamma\).  If \(n<2\) or
\(h/2+\ell/4\geq\delta_0\), use the fallback
\(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{pair}}(x_0)=0\).

In every remaining case, for each unordered pair \(1\leq i<j\leq n\), put
\[
M_{ij}=\frac{X_i+X_j}{2},\qquad
\Delta_{ij}=X_i-X_j,
\qquad
D_{ij}=\frac{(A_i-A_j)(Y_i-Y_j)}2,qquad
W_{ij}=\frac{(A_i-A_j)^2}2,
\]
and \(b_{ij}=b_\gamma((M_{ij}-x_0)/h)\).  Define the pair
\(U\)-statistics
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat Q_{h,\ell}
&=\binom n2^{-1}\sum_{i<j}
K_h(M_{ij}-x_0)K_\ell(\Delta_{ij})
b_{ij}b_{ij}^{\mathsf T}W_{ij},\\
\widehat S_{h,\ell}
&=\binom n2^{-1}\sum_{i<j}
K_h(M_{ij}-x_0)K_\ell(\Delta_{ij})
b_{ij}D_{ij}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Write \(c_0=\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)f_-^2\).  For a symmetric
matrix \(Q=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_j)U^{\mathsf T}\), set
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{pair}}(Q)
=U\operatorname{diag}\!\left(
\min\{f_+^2,\max\{c_0/2,\lambda_j\}\}
\right)U^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Finally define
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,\ell}
=\mathsf C_{\mathrm{pair}}(\widehat Q_{h,\ell})^{-1}
\widehat S_{h,\ell},
\qquad
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{pair}}(x_0)
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-2,2]}
\left\{b_\gamma(0)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\theta_{h,\ell}\right\}.
\]
The half-open convention may be used on one face of each box kernel; the
choice is immaterial on null boundaries.  The spectral map is independent of
the eigenbasis chosen within repeated eigenspaces.  Together with the fixed
polynomial ordering and the stated fallbacks, the construction is a total
measurable function of \(O_{1:n}\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band},n}\), the continuous versions selected by the H\"older restrictions satisfy \[\tau_P(x_0)=\mathbb{E}_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x_0].\]
statements.justification: This selects a law-functional version of the point target before any minimax comparison is made.
statements.gap: The downgraded prior CausalSmith proposal left the unrestricted conditional mean at \(x_0\) version-dependent; the H\"older class used by Kennedy et al. selects a continuous version.
statements.consumer: The minimax risk \(R_n^{\mathrm{band}}\) and every downstream estimator comparison use this identified point target.

statements.statement:
Fix \(d,L,\varepsilon,f_{-},f_{+},x_0\).  Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), there are constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\) such that, for every \(n\geq n_0\),
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{band}}\geq c\,n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
\]
This conclusion is the oracle pointwise-regression branch; it does not assert a density-induced \(n^{-(\alpha+\beta)/d}\) branch under the fixed positive density band.
statements.justification: This is the new information bound showing that an unsmooth observed design law can be first-order for a localized causal functional.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. (2024, Theorem 1 and the following density remark) obtain the faster localized fuzzy-hypothesis lower bound but use a design with holes; no published converse couples density perturbations to the causal nuisances while retaining a fixed positive lower density bound.
statements.consumer: It determines when no density-free pointwise CATE procedure can inherit the known-density KBRW benchmark.
statements.proof_tex:
The asserted inequality is exactly the conclusion of
\(\mathrm{lem:oracle\mbox{-}regression\mbox{-}lower\mbox{-}bound}\).  That
lemma constructs two laws with uniform covariate density, constant propensity
\(1/2\), bounded Rademacher potential outcomes, and CATEs separated at
\(x_0\) by a \(\gamma\)-smooth bump of height
\(c_*n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\).  It verifies membership in
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band},n}\), bounds the one-observation squared Hellinger
distance by \(C n^{-1}\), tensorizes the affinity, and applies the two-point
testing inequality for mean absolute loss.  Its constants are uniform on each
compact subset of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), which gives the quantifiers
in the proposed statement.  Since the pair keeps the density fixed, the proof
establishes only the oracle branch and makes no claim about
\(n^{-(\alpha+\beta)/d}\).

statements.statement: Fix \(d,L,\varepsilon,f_{-},f_{+},x_0\). Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{low}}\), there are constants \(C<\infty\) and \(n_0\) such that for every \(n\ge n_0\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band},n}}\mathbb{E}_P\left|\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{cap}}_n(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|\le C\,\overline r_n^{\mathrm{band}}.\]
statements.justification: This is the strongest proved primitive-class result: an explicit feasible estimator with a density-free mean-risk guarantee.
statements.gap: Kennedy (2023) gives the localized double-residual decomposition under high-level smoother and Gram conditions; this proof verifies those conditions for buffered, rank-capped partition-series fits under the fixed density band.
statements.consumer: It supplies the achievable endpoint of the honest positive-band minimax bracket.

statements.statement:
Under the preceding conditions, uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\),
\[
n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\lesssim R_n^{\mathrm{band}}
\lesssim \overline r_n^{\mathrm{band}}.
\]
Writing \(p=(\alpha+\beta)/d\) and \(q=\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), one has \(0<p<q\) on \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), and hence, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
c n^{-q}\leq R_n^{\mathrm{band}}
\leq C n^{-p}(\log n)^{2p}.
\]
This bracket does not determine a polynomial minimax exponent and does not establish a positive-band slowdown relative to the density-qualified benchmark.
statements.proof_tex:
The proposed version of
\(\mathrm{thm:density\mbox{-}coupled\mbox{-}lower\mbox{-}bound}\) gives
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{band}}\geq c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
\]
The proved rank-capped estimator theorem supplies a single measurable sample
map whose maximal mean absolute error is at most
\(C\overline r_n^{\mathrm{band}}\).  Substituting that map in the infimum in
\(\mathrm{def:band\mbox{-}risk}\) gives
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{band}}\leq C\overline r_n^{\mathrm{band}}.
\]
Both constants are uniform on compact subsets of
\(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), so the first display in the proposed theorem
follows.

Now put \(p=(\alpha+\beta)/d\) and
\(q=\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).  The already established exponent-ordering lemma
gives \(0<p<q\) throughout \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\).  Therefore
\[
n^{-p}(\log n)^{2p}\geq n^{-q}
\]
for every sufficiently large \(n\), and the definition of the upper rate
reduces to
\[
\overline r_n^{\mathrm{band}}
=n^{-p}(\log n)^{2p}.
\]
This proves the displayed bracket.  Because its lower endpoint has exponent
\(q\) and its upper endpoint has the strictly smaller exponent \(p\), the
inequalities permit every possible polynomial exponent between them; they do
not prove that the upper exponent is minimax or that the unknown positive-band
density causes a slowdown.
statements.justification: The corrected theorem records the strongest proved two-sided rate bracket over one primitive positive-band class.
statements.gap: The lower and upper exponents do not match, so the exact positive-band minimax frontier remains open.
statements.consumer: It tells downstream method comparisons exactly which rates are proved and which density-slowdown conclusion is not yet licensed.

statements.statement:
For every \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), define
\[
p=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{d},\qquad
t=\frac{1}{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s)},\qquad
q=\frac{\gamma}{2\gamma+d}.
\]
Then \(0<p<t<q<1/2\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}=n^{-t}\).  Consequently, the additional premise \(R_n^{\mathrm{band}}\geq c n^{-p}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\) would imply
\[
\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{band}}}{r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}}
\geq c n^{t-p}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Without that unproved premise, the available positive-band bracket does not determine the limit of \(R_n^{\mathrm{band}}/r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}\).
statements.proof_tex:
The established lemma
\(\mathrm{lem:low\mbox{-}region\mbox{-}exponent\mbox{-}ordering}\) gives
\(0<p<t<q<1/2\).  By the definition of the benchmark,
\[
r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}=n^{-t}\vee n^{-q}=n^{-t},
\]
because \(t<q\) implies \(n^{-t}>n^{-q}\).  Under the displayed additional
premise in the proposed statement, division by \(n^{-t}\) gives
\[
\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{band}}}{r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}}
\geq c n^{t-p}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
since \(t-p>0\).

On the other hand, the proved positive-band bracket is only
\[
c n^{-q}\leq R_n^{\mathrm{band}}
\leq Cn^{-p}(\log n)^{2p}.
\]
Dividing by \(r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}=n^{-t}\) yields
\[
c n^{t-q}\leq
\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{band}}}{r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}}
\leq Cn^{t-p}(\log n)^{2p}.
\]
The left endpoint tends to zero and the right endpoint tends to infinity.
Thus these proved inequalities imply no limit for the ratio, which is the
final assertion of the proposed statement.
statements.justification: The corrected proposition isolates the valid exponent ordering and the exact missing premise for strict KBRW separation.
statements.gap: No admissible fixed-positive-band converse currently supplies the non-oracle lower branch needed for an unconditional separation.
statements.consumer: It prevents users from interpreting an estimator-side rank cap as an information-theoretic impossibility result.

statements.statement: If \(\pi_P\) and both \(\mu_{a,P}\) are supplied as functions, then the direct plug-in \(\mu_{1,P}(x_0)-\mu_{0,P}(x_0)\) equals \(\tau_P(x_0)\) and has zero error.  Separately, oracleize the corrected weighted local \(R\)-normal equations defining \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{cap}}_n(x_0)\) by replacing their two propensity fits by \(\pi_P\) and their outcome fit by \(\eta_P=\pi_P\mu_{1,P}+(1-\pi_P)\mu_{0,P}\), while retaining the evaluation sample, local-polynomial stage, spectral safeguard, and truncation.  The resulting oracleized estimator has conditional target \(\tau_P\) and, uniformly under the preceding conditions, mean-absolute error \(O(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)})\).
statements.proof_tex:
The direct plug-in assertion follows immediately from the defining identity
\[
\tau_P(x_0)=\mu_{1,P}(x_0)-\mu_{0,P}(x_0).
\]
We prove the nontrivial assertion about the oracleized sample estimator.  Put
\[
\eta_P(x)=\pi_P(x)\mu_{1,P}(x)+(1-\pi_P(x))\mu_{0,P}(x),\qquad
\nu_P(x)=\pi_P(x)\{1-\pi_P(x)\}.
\]
For the oracleized normal equations, define
\[
Z_P=\frac{Y-\eta_P(X)}{A-\pi_P(X)},\qquad
W_P=\{A-\pi_P(X)\}^2.
\]
The denominator is bounded away from zero because \(A\in\{0,1\}\) and
\(\varepsilon\leq\pi_P\leq1-\varepsilon\); bounded outcomes give
\(|Z_P|\leq2/\varepsilon\).  Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[W_PZ_P\mid X]
&=\mathbb E_P[(A-\pi_P(X))(Y-\eta_P(X))\mid X]\\
&=\pi_P(X)\{1-\pi_P(X)\}\{\mu_{1,P}(X)-\mu_{0,P}(X)\}\\
&=\nu_P(X)\tau_P(X),\\
\mathbb E_P[W_P\mid X]&=\nu_P(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the weighted conditional regression function of \(Z_P\) is exactly
\(\tau_P\), not a newly defined estimand.

With \(h_n=n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)}\), the oracleized evaluation equations are
weighted local-polynomial normal equations for this regression, with the
monomial vector through degree \(\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\).  Their population
local Gram matrix is an integral against
\(\nu_P(x)f_P(x)\).  Density-band and overlap bounds give
\[
\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)f_-\leq
\nu_P(x)f_P(x)\leq f_+/4,
\]
so its eigenvalues are bounded above and below by positive constants depending
only on the fixed polynomial moment matrix and the displayed class constants.
The spectral safeguard in the corrected construction is therefore inactive
whenever the empirical Gram differs from its expectation by less than half
the population lower eigenvalue.  A direct independence and second-moment
calculation, entry by entry in the fixed-dimensional Gram matrix, bounds the
probability of the complementary event by \(C/(nh_n^d)\).

On the good-Gram event, the Taylor polynomial of \(\tau_P\) at \(x_0\) has
uniform remainder at most \(CLh_n^\gamma\).  Substitution in the weighted
normal equations therefore bounds the deterministic approximation part of
the fitted intercept by \(Ch_n^\gamma\).  Conditional on the design and
treatments, the centered summands
\[
W_P\{Z_P-\tau_P(X)\}
\]
are uniformly bounded and have conditional mean zero after averaging over
treatment and outcome at each covariate.  The local Gram bounds then give
variance at most \(C/(nh_n^d)\) for the fitted intercept.  Jensen's inequality
turns this into mean absolute noise at most \(C(nh_n^d)^{-1/2}\).  Truncation
to \([-2,2]\) cannot increase error and makes the bad-Gram contribution at
most \(C/(nh_n^d)\).  Hence
\[
\mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{or}}(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)|
\leq C\left\{h_n^\gamma+(nh_n^d)^{-1/2}+(nh_n^d)^{-1}\right\}
\leq Cn^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
\]
The calculation uses only the fixed density band, overlap, bounded outcomes,
H\"older CATE condition, and independent sampling, so the constant is uniform
over the stated class and compact smoothness subsets.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check that the new frontier retains the classical oracle regression branch.
statements.gap: The new density-coupled argument must not manufacture a slowdown when the causal nuisances are supplied; this reduction pins down that boundary case.
statements.consumer: It lets local-polynomial CATE theory and software recover the standard random-design regression rate as a direct special case.

statements.statement:
Under no regularity on \(f_P\) beyond \(f_{-}\leq f_P\leq f_{+}\), determine the exact minimax exponent and a matching positive-band converse on
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\cap
\{(\alpha,\beta,\gamma):0<\beta<\alpha\leq1\},
\]
where the proved close-pair upper endpoint is \(n^{-t}\), the available oracle lower endpoint is \(n^{-q}\), and \(t<q\).  Then determine whether the logarithmic factor in the broader rank-capped upper bound can be removed on the remainder of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), and characterize the corresponding band-only frontier for the opposite ordering \(\alpha<\beta\).  Benchmark-rate achievability on the displayed close-pair region is settled; exact minimaxity and the remaining orderings are not presupposed.
statements.justification: The exact positive-band rate and even the existence of a density-induced slowdown remain unresolved after the honest bracket.
statements.gap: The available converse is only the oracle pointwise-regression branch, while the feasible rank-capped upper endpoint contains an unmatched nuisance branch.
statements.consumer: A resolution would determine whether the design density is first order and whether one procedure is minimax across both nuisance-smoothness orderings.

sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. observational random-design experiment with an unknown Lebesgue density satisfying only the fixed band \(f_-\leq f_P\leq f_+\); no density smoothness or estimability condition is imposed.
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes \(O=(Y,A,X)\), with \(X\in[0,1]^d\) and bounded potential outcomes.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is binary and conditionally exchangeable given \(X\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The close-pair estimator fits neither the propensity, outcome regressions, nor the design density; it uses all unordered sample pairs with explicit midpoint and distance bandwidths.  On the broader low-smoothness region, the fallback uses cross-fitted partition-series nuisance regressions capped at \(k_n=\lfloor n/(\log n)^2\rfloor\).  Neither method estimates \(f_P\) or assumes a density modulus.

estimand_functional:
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}=\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\cap
\{(\alpha,\beta,\gamma):0<\beta<\alpha\leq1\},
\qquad
t=\left(1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{4s}\right)^{-1},
\qquad
q=\frac{\gamma}{2\gamma+d}.
\]
Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\), the total close-pair estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band},n}}
\mathbb E_P\left|\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{pair}}(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|
\lesssim n^{-t}=r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}},
\]
using only \(f_-\leq f_P\leq f_+\), without estimating \(f_P\) or assuming density smoothness.  Together with the oracle pointwise-regression lower branch,
\[
n^{-q}\lesssim R_n^{\mathrm{band}}\lesssim n^{-t},
\qquad t<q.
\]
The distinct endpoints leave the exact band-only minimax exponent and a matching positive-band converse open.  On \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), the broader rank-capped fallback remains
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band},n}}
\mathbb E_P\left|\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{cap}}(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|
\lesssim\overline r_n^{\mathrm{band}}.
\]
If \(\pi_P,\mu_{0,P},\mu_{1,P}\) are supplied, the direct plug-in \(\mu_{1,P}(x_0)-\mu_{0,P}(x_0)\) has zero error.  Separately, oracleizing the local \(R\)-normal equations while retaining their evaluation sample gives mean absolute error \(O(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)})\)
target_estimand: The observed-data target is \(\tau_P(x_0)=\mu_{1,P}(x_0)-\mu_{0,P}(x_0)\).  Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, overlap, and the continuous-version convention in \(\mathrm{lem:cate\mbox{-}identification}\), this same point target equals the causal estimand \(\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x_0]\).  The statistical contribution concerns estimation risk for this target over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band},n}\); the benchmark rate and minimax frontier are comparison objects, not alternative estimands

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman give the benchmark formula and a lower construction over a broader density-above model, while matching achievability uses additional covariate-law or density control; their Section~3 \(\delta_3\) flat-top construction has support holes and is not a converse for the fixed-positive-band class.

Kennedy's local-polynomial doubly robust analysis attains a benchmark-rate lane under high-level nuisance-smoother and Gram conditions; the close-pair theorem instead verifies a primitive fixed-band upper bound without density fitting on \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\).

Empirical inverse-Gram higher-order estimators remove density smoothness for global average functionals when the projection dimension is below sample size; this informs only the broader rank-capped fallback.
Same-sample stabilization controls global bilinear forms at sublinear projection dimension and motivates, but does not solve, the remaining asymmetric band-only frontier.

Shen--Gao--Witten--Han are the nearest construction precedent for two-bandwidth pair-difference U-statistics without design-density smoothness; the causal pair identity and midpoint-symmetric nuisance remainder in the close-pair theorem are specific to the present CATE problem.

tldr: A total close-pair local \(R\)-estimator attains the Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman benchmark rate on the nonempty region \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\) using only the fixed density band \(f_{-}\leq f_P\leq f_{+}\), with no density estimator or density smoothness.  The proved positive-band minimax bracket is \(c n^{-q}\leq R_n^{\mathrm{band}}\leq Cn^{-t}=Cr_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}\) with \(t<q\), so exact minimaxity and a matching positive-band converse remain open.  A broader rank-capped estimator gives the stated logarithmically inflated upper bound on \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\).

project_justification.gap: The density-qualified pointwise CATE benchmark is known, but under only a fixed positive band on an otherwise arbitrary design density there was no primitive, density-free estimator verification at that benchmark and there is still no matching positive-band converse.  Existing empirical higher-order influence-function results concern global functionals or projection dimensions below the relevant sample rank and do not determine this localized frontier.
project_justification.niche: On \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\), midpoint localization and sufficiently close covariate pairs turn treatment and outcome differences into a local \(R\)-normal equation whose nuisance remainder is of order \(\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\).  The two-sided density band alone gives population rank and the pairwise Hoeffding variance calculation, so density smoothness is unnecessary for benchmark-rate achievability.
project_justification.fill: The note constructs a total pair-difference \(U\)-statistic estimator and proves the compact-uniform risk bound \(h^\gamma+\ell^{\alpha+\beta}+(nh^d)^{-1/2}+(n^2h^d\ell^d)^{-1/2}\), optimized at \(n^{-t}=r_n^{\mathrm{KBRW}}\).  It combines this estimator with the oracle pointwise-regression lower branch to give the honest bracket \(c n^{-q}\leq R_n^{\mathrm{band}}\leq Cn^{-t}\), while retaining the broader rank-capped fallback outside the close-pair region.

related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) provide the pointwise CATE benchmark formula and a density-qualified construction; their flat-top lower construction has support holes and therefore is not a converse for the present fixed-positive-band class.  Kennedy (2023) develops local-polynomial doubly robust CATE estimation under high-level nuisance-smoother and Gram conditions.  Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2017), and Liu, Li, Gu, and Liu (2026), motivate empirical or stabilized Gram replacement for global bilinear functionals, but do not settle the localized asymmetric frontier here.  Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020) are the closest random-design precedent for pair-difference \(U\)-statistics without density smoothness; the causal pair identity and midpoint-symmetric remainder used here are specific to CATE estimation.  Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2016) concern quadratic-estimator limit theory rather than this pointwise minimax exponent.
technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved step is information-theoretic, not merely a rank calculation.  A matching converse must construct laws that retain \(f_P\geq f_->0\), satisfy the unequal nuisance H\"older restrictions, separate \(\tau_P(x_0)\) at the \(n^{-t}\) scale, and keep the corresponding \(n\)-sample mixtures close.  The candidate density-coupled program has not verified these properties.  Log removal outside \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\) also remains unresolved, and \(\alpha<\beta\) lies outside the currently defined \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\).
honest_scope: The proved headline is benchmark-rate achievability, without density estimation or density smoothness, on the nonempty close-pair region.  The strongest minimax conclusion there is the loose bracket \(c n^{-q}\leq R_n^{\mathrm{band}}\leq Cn^{-t}\) with \(t<q\); exact positive-band minimaxity and a matching converse are not claimed.  On the remainder of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{low}}\), only the oracle lower branch and the logarithmically inflated rank-capped upper bound are proved.  The opposite nuisance ordering requires a newly defined regime.  If the outcome regressions are supplied, direct plug-in has zero error; oracleizing only the local normal equations while retaining the evaluation sample gives the classical pointwise-regression rate.
